title: Crimp terminations as parts: contacts, seals and tooling per cavity

Connectors carry a construction (crimp) but no contacts: a crimp housing with loose contacts, wire seals, cavity plugs and the applicator/tool cannot be recorded, so the BOM and build sheet miss them. title: Change history for the database backend: browse and restore change sets
description: Rank 4 (degraded). The prior studio committed every save to git with the author, so history was a git log away. In WireHub the git export works only on the file backend; on the default Postgres backend history lives in change_set/change rows with no UI and no export of history (GET /api/export is a snapshot). Add: a History panel per design and per library record (who, when, what changed, the diff), a hub-wide recent-changes list, restore-a-record-to-this-change (a new change set, never a rewrite), and optionally a git mirror job that writes each change set as a commit to a configured remote.
acceptance_criteria: On pg a user sees the history of a record and of the hub, opens a diff and restores an earlier state as a new change set; RLS respected; optional git mirror documented in self-hosting.md; contract tests on both backends where meaningful.
notes: Built on feat/change-history: /api/history (hub list with person/date/kind filters, per-record history, entry detail with before/after, restore as a new change set via the design/definition routes under edit lock and quoted versions); pg source from change_set/change + migration 0017 change.before_body; files source from the git log of the catalog dir (none without git); History drawer on cables (top bar) and library records, /history page; opt-in git-mirror worker job (WIREHUB_GIT_MIRROR_*). Tests: files+pg scenario, DOM, mirror on pg. Follow-ups cs-5k1.25, cs-5k1.26.

title: Part-number health: duplicates, unnumbered parts, disagreements
description: Rank 3 (missing, generic). The prior studio reconciled numbers against a private register and never reused one; WireHub only checks the format. Nothing warns when two records or two designs carry the same part number, or lists what has none. Add: validateDb warning pn-duplicate (same canonical PN on two records that are not body/connector twins); PartNumberField warns when the typed number is taken; a report (Library filter and cable-list filter, or a small page) of unnumbered parts/designs, duplicates, and designs whose productRef disagrees with their drawing PN. Goes through PartNumberScheme.parse for canonical forms.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate numbers raise a warning in validation and in the field; the report lists unnumbered, duplicate and disagreeing items on the starter catalog fixtures; no numbering pattern hard-coded.
notes: Also: the Library PN column tooltip (library-table.ts) still says 'or the register's' though the base has no register; and the cable list no longer shows a faint suggested number for an unnumbered design (the suggestion moved to the PN field) - the report covers that.

title: Organisation identity on documents without a module
description: Rank 2 (degraded). The prior studio printed its organisation on every sheet. WireHub prints WireHub on the wire spec, an empty rights line and no logo on the drawing sheet, and only a code module (registerDrawingArt, WireSpecOptions) can change that. Add a hub setting (setup step and an admin settings panel; stored with the catalog, both backends): organisation name, standard name and file prefix for the wire spec, title-block logo (PNG/SVG upload, sanitised), rights/confidentiality line, default designer, title-block general note and tolerances. Feeds the drawing sheet, wire spec, build sheet and BOM header. Coordinate with cs-ml3 (standards profiles) so a profile can override.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh hub sets name, logo and rights line in the UI and every document shows them; unset values keep todays generic text; module art still wins over the setting; tests on both backends.

title: Backrest post-snapshot hook touches the backup marker GC and the deep check read

title: Drawing standards profiles: ISO and ASME conventions for exported drawings and documents
description:
Owner 2026-10-05: exported schematics/drawings/documents follow no formal standard today (no ISO/ASME claims; only data citations like IEC 60807-3). Add selectable standards profiles per org/design:
- ISO profile: ISO 5457 sheet sizes/frames, ISO 7200 title block fields, ISO 128 line types/lettering, ISO 129-1 dimensioning, first-angle projection symbol, ISO 81346 reference designations.
- ASME profile: ASME Y14.1 sheet sizes (A-E), Y14.100 drawing practices and title block, Y14.5 dimensioning/tolerancing, Y14.35 revision block, Y14.24 drawing type (wire harness), third-angle projection symbol, Y14.44 reference designations.
- Schematic symbols: IEC 60617 (ISO profile) or IEEE 315 (ASME profile).
- Harness/build docs: IPC/WHMA-A-620 acceptance class (1/2/3) on build sheet and test spec; continuity/hipot test spec structured to A-620 test requirements.
- Wire/cable identification: IEC 62491 / SAE AS50881-style marking where applicable.
- Revision control on every sheet (rev letter, ECO/change history from change sets).
Deliver as conventions WireHub follows ('follows ISO 7200 fields'), not certification claims; verify against the actual standard texts before claiming. Module hook so a deployment can supply its own house profile/title block. Depends on the drawing-language spec (cs-48a).

title: Costing: part prices and BOM cost roll-up
description: Rank 17 (gap beyond parity). Components can name suppliers but there are no prices, MOQ or currency, so a BOM has no cost. Add optional price breaks per supplier on part records and a cost column and total on the BOM per length variation and build quantity; a module may supply live pricing.

title: Harness formboard drawing for branched assemblies

Breakouts model branch points but there is no 1:1 formboard/nailboard drawing with bundle lengths between branch points, branch angles and labels, which a harness shop builds on. Add a formboard sheet type derived from breakouts and segment lengths (scale, tiled pages), following the drawing-language spec.
acceptance_criteria: A starter breakout design prints a formboard with dimensioned branch lengths at 1:1 or a stated scale; deterministic SVG golden.

title: Electrical rules: gauge, contact rating and voltage drop
description: Rank 15 (gap beyond parity). Nothing checks that a conductor can carry the current its pins carry, that a contact is rated for the wire, or the voltage drop over the length. Add optional per-signal or per-net current (vocabulary signal kinds can carry a default), conductor area to ampacity (cited table, flagged inferred where so), contact current rating, and warnings plus a summary on the continuity spec.
acceptance_criteria: With currents declared, an undersized conductor or contact warns with the cited rule; voltage drop shown per net with length; no warnings when nothing is declared.

title: Re-specify the remaining dropped design specs generically
description: Rank 14 (missing, generic: documentation). boundaries.md section 5 dropped seven specs as full of private examples and promised to re-specify them generically; only the drawing language was (cs-48a). Missing: design versions and locking (snapshot format, frozen definitions, artwork copies, unlock/relock history), shield bonding and pigtails, the schematic visual language, depictions and anchors, the library tables and record pages, and the workbench UX rules (no JSON as primary UI, provenance as input, plain-language errors). Write them under specs/ with synthetic examples.
acceptance_criteria: specs/ holds generic versions, shield-bonding, schematic and library/workbench specs that match the code; privacy check clean; boundaries.md section 5 updated.

title: Decide: public board-import module for open file formats (KiCad, Gerber, fab BOM/CPL)
description: Rank 13 (owner decision; private by design today). boundaries.md left the board importers private because they read one file share layout. The file formats are public: a KiCad .kicad_pcb/netlist gives terminals, pads and internal links; a Gerber set renders board art; a fab BOM/CPL lists board components. A public module over the importer contract (user uploads files, review and publish as a job) would serve any shop. Decide whether to build it publicly; if yes, split into module beads (KiCad PCB/netlist to PCBA, Gerber to depiction, BOM/CPL to components).
acceptance_criteria: Owner decision recorded; if yes, module beads filed under this epic and boundaries.md gains a row for the public module.
close_reason: Decided: build it public. modules/board-import (MIT) on feat/board-import-module: kicad-board (.kicad_pcb/.net -> PCBA + kicad art), gerbers (.zip -> gerber art, anchored), fab-bom (.csv/.board-bom.json -> components + board parts), page /m/board-import/boards. Importer contract extended (options, boardParts, depictions). boundaries.md §10.1 and feature row record it. Follow-ups cs-5k1.29-.32.

title: KiCad 3D models: give the board-model and library-model pipeline a way in, or remove it
description: Rank 12 (degraded). The server keeps the KiCad board-assembly path (models/kicad-pcb.ts, assembly.ts, kicad-library.ts, model source kind kicad-board) but the import-models and kicad-fetch scripts that fed it were left behind, so nothing in the base can create those sources; comments still name the missing scripts. Either (a) accept a .kicad_pcb upload as a model source for a PCBA and fetch the pinned kicad-packages3D files it names in a model-cache job, or (b) move the path into the board-import module and drop it here. Fix the stale comments either way.
acceptance_criteria: Either a board record gets a 3D model from an uploaded .kicad_pcb end to end (job, cache, viewer) with a test, or the dead code is removed and boundaries.md updated; no comment names a script that is not in the repo.
close_reason: Option (a): POST /api/models/pcbas/:id/upload accepts a .kicad_pcb, kept as data/model-sources/<sha>.kicad_pcb.txt, link build {assembly, library: pinned commit}; model-cache job fetches kicad-packages3D files into the cache (library-source.ts), never committed. Tested end to end on files and pg (stand-in library). Stale script mentions removed.

title: Release approvals on saved versions
description: Rank 11 (gap beyond parity). Saving a version locks it with a note, but there is no review or sign-off: no approver, no approval state, no change description on the sheet revision block. Add optional approval: a saved version can be submitted, approved or rejected by a person with the right role; documents print approver and date; the drawing revision block lists the version notes. Ties into cs-ml3 (revision block conventions).
acceptance_criteria: With approvals enabled a version shows draft/approved state and approver; only approved versions print without the UNRELEASED/UNAPPROVED mark; audit recorded in version history; role check on both backends.

Add a Make-variant menu and command (Copy onto another stock...: pick a compatible stock, preview the moved conductors, create the copy via the duplicate lifecycle). Also fix the stale EditorCommands header comment that still lists the dropped variants.
acceptance_criteria: The menu offers only stocks canSwapTrunkStock accepts; the copy is a new design with the trunk moved by conductor colour; dom test; no shop wording.

title: Sub-assemblies: a design that uses other designs as parts

Add a design instance kind that places another design (by id and optionally a saved revision) with its exposed ends as terminals, BOM roll-up (one line or exploded), where-used across designs, and versions freezing the referenced revision.
acceptance_criteria: A design places another design, traces through it, rolls it up in the BOM and freezes its revision on save version; validation catches cycles; schema version bumped with migration.
notes: Built on feat/sub-assemblies: model subassemblies.ts (instances.subassemblies, schema v5, ports = connector pins + flying leads + nested free ports, flattenSubassemblies, cycle/missing/rev/port validation, pinSubassemblies on save version, Db.assemblies library); docs (one BOM line by productRef/rev with explode option and cost roll-up, build sheet references the sub's sheet, continuity/schematic/formboard flattened); editor (block node with ports, palette placement via AssembliesAdapter, inspector open + pin/unpin); studio (/api/assemblies, /api/designs/:id/used-in, cable-list chips, delete/rename refused, version freeze, ?explode=1, pg ref_edge role subassembly + S1 gate check); starter dc-pigtail-lead + dc-y-from-leads.

title: Connect known pins: propose the joints a partly wired design lacks

Show the proposals in a dialog to accept per row; one undo step.
acceptance_criteria: On a starter design with joints removed the command proposes exactly the removed unambiguous joints and lists the ambiguous ones without proposing them; works through the vocabulary only (no hard-coded signal names); dom test.
